analysis: The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md: the 'Last updated' stamp moves from 2026-10-22 to 2026-10-23 (line 3), and a new paragraph is added after line 172 describing two test names (`returnedAssistantReasoningRendersLikeReasoningContent`, `openRouterReasoningContentReturnRequestsAreServed`) that push OpenRouter's returned-reasoning tool turn through the coordinator and local HTTP paths to the rendered prompt. This is documentation of test coverage. It changes no runtime code, keys, attestation, authorization, cache storage, WebSocket contract, or fan helper behavior. I checked the change against the threat model (T-041 prefix cache, TB-002/TB-011 boundaries, A-001 prompt confidentiality). None are affected: no production setting is loosened, and no secrets, endpoints or credentials are introduced. The unchanged surrounding text keeps its caveats about isolated state and never targeting production, and the new text adds no instruction that would weaken them. Unverified: whether the named tests exist in the source tree and exercise what the docs claim. That is a documentation-accuracy question outside the supplied evidence, not a security regression. The sibling test files are not in this batch. The reasoning-return handling in the actual provider/prompt code is not reviewed here, so the next pass should examine any code PR that adds it, in particular for reasoning content leaking into logs or plaintext paths (T-008, A-001).
